chunks: Muhammad b. al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. al-Hasan b. Aban narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Sa'id from al-Nadr b. Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Muhammad b. Marwan from Sa'd b. Turayf from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir from his father from his grandfather (upon them be peace). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said: Whoever recites ten verses in a night will not be recorded among the heedless. Whoever recites fifty verses will be recorded among those who remember. Whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among the devoutly obedient. Whoever recites two hundred verses will be recorded among the humble. Whoever recites three hundred verses will be recorded among the winners. Whoever recites five hundred verses will be recorded among the strivers. Whoever recites one thousand verses will be assigned a qintar; and the qintar is fifty thousand gold weights, and each weight is twenty-four carats — the smallest of which is like Mount Uhud, and the largest of which is like what is between heaven and earth.

key_terms.الخاشعين: the humble, those with inner reverence
key_terms.الغافلين: the heedless, those who neglect worship
key_terms.المجتهدين: the strivers, those who exert utmost effort

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for reciting different numbers of Quran verses at night?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad establishes a graduated scale of spiritual rewards for nightly Quran recitation. Starting from just ten verses (which saves one from heedlessness), the rewards escalate through remembrance (50), devout obedience (100), humility (200), triumph (300), and striving (500), culminating in a qintar for 1,000 verses — an enormous treasure described in vivid material terms to convey immeasurable divine reward. Each level uses a Quranic descriptor of the righteous, encouraging all believers to recite according to their capacity.
